newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: CamGSM launches Cambodian Global System Mobile.
newsitem.headline: CamGSM launches Cambodian Global System Mobile.

text.p: CamGSM Company Ltd on Tuesday formally launched its $50 million MobiTel venture to provide Cambodia's first digital mobile cellular telephone service.

"Cambodia is now on the GSM (Global System Mobile) map," Hakan Ledin, vice-chairman and executive director of Millicom International Cellular SA, told an inaugration ceremony for the firm's Phnom Penh offices attended by co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Ledin said the venture, which has spent $13 million to date, would eventually invest a total of about $50 million and provide services to more than 10,000 subscribers.

CamGSM is a joint venture between Royal Millicom and the Ministry of Post and Telecommunications. Royal Millicom is a joint venture between Luxembourg-based Millicom International Cellular SA and the Royal Group, a Cambodian company.

Company representatives said GSM provided clearer lines, protection against theft of telephone numbers, caller identification, voice mail, call forwarding and roaming, which allows customers to receive calls in other nations.
A roaming service with Singapore and Hong Kong is expected to be on line by May.

After decades of war in Cambodia, telecommunications are woefully inadequate, and mobile companies have flooded into the market to compensate for the lack of fixed lines, which numbered only 6,000 in the early 1990s.

The government was recently forced to temporarily suspend licences for new players in an attempt to allow existing ventures, including analog service providers Samart, Camtel and Tricelcam, to operate more efficiently, said Minister of Posts and Telecommunications So Khun.
He said that in addition to MobiTel, which was granted its licence in April 1996, Samart has been granted a GSM licence. Samart will be permitted to provide a service in 18 months, he said.
